emergent_bug.violated_requirement: ρ = atomic([read(tp->copied_seq)]) from thread_a (the lockless poll read of the seq cursor must not interleave with a conflicting write)
emergent_bug.missing_guarantee: thread_b updates copied_seq while holding the socket lock, but tcp_poll deliberately does NOT lock the socket; a one-sided socket lock does not serialize the lockless poll read → no g establishes atomic(read) on the reader side
emergent_bug.category_rationale: ρ is atomic over a single access (an unmarked lockless read concurrent with a conflicting write) → data race / store-tearing

fix_maps_to: READ_ONCE(tp->copied_seq) added to all lockless readers (tcp_stream_is_readable, tcp_poll, diag) and WRITE_ONCE on all writers/initializers (tcp_recvmsg, tcp_read_sock, tcp_disconnect, state-setup, child create) → marks the accesses so they are single well-defined accesses (establishes atomic(read/write) at the C-memory-model level)
recall_risk_notes: Structurally identical to a one-sided-lock poll race; the unprotected reader yields atomic(read) directly and threads/object are static-friendly (well-known .poll/.recvmsg ops on one struct field). Risk: this is a benign word-tearing race on a heuristic seq cursor (writer is socket-locked, reader intentionally lockless), so an LLM may judge the poll read benign and decline to assert atomic(read), suppressing the report. Many additional writer sites across files, but only one is needed for the conflict.
